text: grain-ingest is running, but nothing yet stops any other pod in the namespace from reaching Azure SQL directly. A pre-harvest security review flags it, and this video closes the gap fast.
A default-deny NetworkPolicy, plus a narrow rule allowing database access only from pods labeled app: ingest — applied straight through kubectl, ahead of the Helm chart's own review queue.
That selector comes from an older security runbook, written before the Helm chart existed under the service's earlier name — and it's never diffed against the Deployment Lesson 9 actually shipped.

The policy is tested the way a NetworkPolicy gets tested in isolation: a disposable pod hand-labeled to match the rule connects successfully; relabeled, it's blocked. Both results are correct, so the fix ships, verified.
What never gets tested is a connection from an actual grain-ingest pod — the ones carrying a different label entirely. That gap stays invisible for now.
